IEA (2024). The Future of Geothermal Energy. International Energy Agency, Paris, December 2024. Special report prepared by the IEA Directorate of Energy Markets and Security and Directorate of Sustainability, Technology and Outlooks, with technical-potential modelling by Project InnerSpace. https://www.iea.org/reports/the-future-of-geothermal-energy. Licence: CC BY 4.0.

Targeted pass for geothermal-well_* and heat supply. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed page). Region: global (some EU/US figures). Money: the report uses 2023 USD at market exchange rates (chart axes and notes say 'USD (2023, MER)'); where a value sits in a section whose chart is labelled 2023 USD, 2023_USD is used and the note says so; where a table or passage gives no year (Ch.1 heat costs; Ch.2 assumption table), 2024_USD with 'PRICE YEAR NOT STATED'. Main file: conventional hydrothermal power LCOE and fleet capacity factor; conventional direct-use heat cost range and district-heating capex (USD 3 000/kW); well lifetime 20-30 years; EGS technical-potential assumptions (power capex 2 250/kW surface plant only, opex 2% of capex, lifetime 20/25 years, capacity factor 80/90%, 6 years derisking and construction); next-generation EGS power capex and LCOE for first-of-a-kind, 2035 and 2050 (low-medium ranges, 300 MW, WACC 7%); next-generation industrial heat capex (1 150-3 150 USD/kWth = subsurface 1 000-3 000 + plant 150), LCOH 2035 and 2050, maximum about 200 degC; the district-heating LCOH figure: geothermal CHP capex 2035/2050 and comparator capex ranges (gas CHP, gas CHP+CCUS, coal CHP, coal CHP+CCUS, bioenergy CHP, nuclear CHP, large heat pumps), with LCOH where the text prints it, 80% utilisation, 7% WACC, 95% capture, heat pump COP 3.8-4.1. Other-values: technical-potential model inputs (wells, flow, drilling USD 2 000/m, stimulation USD 2 800/m), capex/LCOE shares, cost-reduction percentages, total project investments, closed-loop demonstration data. Not loaded: technical potential (TW/EJ), market potential, investment totals, policy chapters, storage and lithium sections. Traps: (1) the district-heating figure prints CAPEX labels in one row under nine bars; the pairing (geothermal 3 600-8 400 and 2 100-4 900, then seven min-max pairs) was inferred from label order and checked against the nuclear text (USD 2 000-6 000/kW); comparators are not split by year. (2) 'USD/kW' for CHP and heat pumps is not labelled kWe or kWth; capacity bases are assumptions stated in the notes. (3) The EGS 'up to USD 15 000/kW in 2024' sentence follows a district-heating sentence; power basis assumed. (4) Industrial-heat costs are derived by the IEA from electricity-application data at 2 kWth/kWe.
